title: Advanced Trampoline with Deformable Mesh & Scoring
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an advanced 3D trampoline physics simulation using Three.js. The scene features a deformable trampoline mesh and a Ferrari model (loaded from 'ferrari.glb' using GLTFLoader from CDN) that bounces on the trampoline with realistic physics and a scoring system.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 15) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (5, 15, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Skybox: use a gradient background from light blue (#87CEEB) at top to white at bottom (or set scene background to #87CEEB).
- Ground plane: large flat plane at y=-0.1, green color (#2d5a27), receives shadows.

## Trampoline Construction
- Create a circular trampoline frame using a TorusGeometry (radius 4, tube 0.3) with metallic dark gray material, positioned at y=2.
- 8 trampoline legs: CylinderGeometry pillars from y=0 to y=2, evenly spaced around the frame.
- Deformable trampoline surface: Create a CircleGeometry (radius 3.8, 64 segments) as a PlaneGeometry alternative — actually use a PlaneGeometry(7.6, 7.6, 32, 32) clipped to a circle. The mesh surface should be blue (#1a5276) with double-sided rendering. Store original vertex positions. The surface deforms when the Ferrari lands on it — vertices within a radius of impact get pushed downward proportionally (Gaussian falloff). The deformation recovers over time (spring-back with damping factor 0.92 per frame).

## Ferrari Model
- Load 'ferrari.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale the model to fit approximately 1.5 units wide. Position initially at (0, 12, 0) above the trampoline.
- The Ferrari acts as the bouncing object. Apply gravity (9.81 m/s²) with dt=1/60.
- On collision with trampoline surface (when Ferrari y <= trampolineSurfaceY + ferrariBoundingHeight/2), apply bounce: velocity.y = -velocity.y * restitution (restitution = 0.85). Each bounce deforms the trampoline mesh at the impact point.
- Add air resistance: velocity *= 0.998 per frame.
- The Ferrari can be launched upward by pressing SPACE (adds +8 to velocity.y if currently on or near trampoline).
- Arrow keys LEFT/RIGHT apply horizontal force (acceleration ±0.15 per frame) to move Ferrari laterally. Clamp x position to [-5, 5].
- Arrow UP/DOWN move Ferrari along z-axis similarly. Clamp z to [-5, 5].

## Scoring System
- Each bounce scores points based on: max height reached since last bounce × 10, rounded to integer.
- Combo system: consecutive bounces within 3 seconds of each other increment a combo multiplier (starts at 1, increments by 1 per consecutive bounce, max 10).
- If more than 3 seconds pass without a bounce, combo resets to 1.
- A 'trick' bonus: if the Ferrari is moving horizontally (|vx| > 1 or |vz| > 1) during a bounce, add 50 bonus points × combo multiplier.
- Track total score, current combo, bounce count, and max height achieved.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left: 'Score: {score}' in white, 24px bold font, with text shadow.
- Top-right: 'Combo: x{combo}' — turns gold (#FFD700) when combo >= 5.
- Center-top: 'Bounce #{count}' displayed briefly (fade out over 1 second) after each bounce.
- Bottom-center: 'Max Height: {maxHeight}m' in white.
- A 'Reset' button (id='resetBtn') at bottom-right that resets Ferrari to (0, 12, 0), resets score/combo/bounces to 0, and restores trampoline mesh.
- A 'Gravity' slider (id='gravitySlider', range 1-20, default 9.81) that adjusts gravity in real-time.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- ferrariPosition: {x, y, z} — current Ferrari position
- ferrariVelocity: {x, y, z} — current velocity
- trampolineDeformation: number — max current deformation depth of any vertex (positive = downward)
- score: number — total score
- combo: number — current combo multiplier
- bounceCount: number — total bounces
- maxHeight: number — highest y the Ferrari has reached
- gravity: number — current gravity value
- isOnTrampoline: boolean — true if Ferrari is in contact with trampoline
- lastBounceTime: number — timestamp (ms) of last bounce
- trickBonusActive: boolean — true if last bounce awarded trick bonus
- modelLoaded: boolean — true once Ferrari GLB is loaded
- simRunning: boolean — true when simulation is active
- meshVertexCount: number — number of vertices in deformable trampoline mesh
- totalEnergy: number — approximate total mechanical energy (0.5*m*v² + m*g*h, mass=1)

## Physics Details
- Use frame-based Euler integration: position += velocity * dt; velocity.y -= gravity * dt.
- Trampoline surface at y=2. Bounce detection when ferrariPosition.y <= 2 + halfHeight.
- On bounce, also apply a small upward impulse from trampoline deformation recovery.
- Ensure no NaN values in any state field at any time.
- Energy should decrease over time due to air resistance and imperfect restitution (never increase spontaneously without SPACE press).

Make sure the simulation starts automatically after model load. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop.
physics_constraints: Euler integration with gravity (configurable 1-20 m/s²), restitution coefficient 0.85, air drag 0.998/frame, Gaussian mesh deformation with spring-back damping 0.92/frame. Energy must monotonically decrease unless external impulse (SPACE). No NaN in any state variable. Horizontal clamping to [-5,5]. Combo resets after 3s without bounce.
